text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal X-ray: Dilated loops of bowel with no gas in the rectum, suggestive of a distal obstruction. Rectal Biopsy: Absence of ganglion cells in the submucosa and myenteric plexus, consistent with Hirschsprung’s disease.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Inability to pass meconium, Abdominal distension. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The combination of delayed meconium passage, bilious vomiting, and abdominal distension in a newborn is highly suggestive of Hirschsprung disease. I will review the pending abdominal X-ray and rectal biopsy results to confirm the absence of ganglion cells.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung disease
